Comprehensive Summary  
 
2,3-Allenyl amines have shown wide applicability in biomedical and synthetic applications. Due to their enormous potential for appli-
cations, researchers have been dedicated to the development of methods  for synthesizing 2,3 -allenyl amines. Herein, a palladi-
um-catalyzed three-component reaction of 2 -alkynyl-1,4-diol dicarbonates, or ganoboronic acids, and nitrogen nucleophiles forming 
2,3-allenyl amines with excellent regio- and chemo-selectivity has been developed. Substrate compatibility and synthetic applications 
have been demonstrated. Control experiments supported a mechanism inv olving 1,2,3-triene-Pd species and methylene-π-allyl palla-
dium species.

Background and Originality Content 
2,3-Allenyl amines have been attracting attention due to their 
application prospects.[1-2] Traditional approaches to form 2,3-allenyl 
amines applying nitrogen nucleophiles are two-component reac-
tions between amines and enynes, [3] 2-(pseudo)halo-1,3-dienes,[4] 
and allenes [5] (Scheme 1a) . Our group recently developed the 
Pd-catalyzed three-component coupling reaction of 2 -alkynyl-1,4- 
diol dicarbonates, organoboronic acids, and malonate or 
bis(phenylsulfonyl)methane anions, which afforded trisubstituted 
allenes in excellent chemo- and regio -selectivity (Sche me 1b). [6] 
On the selection of nucleophiles, carbon nucleophiles such as 
malonates and bis(phenylsulfonyl)methane gave up to 91% yields, 
however, nitrogen nucleophiles are limited to Bn 2NH while other 
benzyl- and allyl- amines didn’t work. Herein, we wish to report a 
Pd-catalyzed three -component coupling reaction yielding 
2,3-allenyl amines from 2 -alkynyl-1,4-diol dicarbonates, organo -
boronic acids, and nitrogen nucleophile s with an excellent selec -
tivity (Scheme 1c).  
Scheme 1   Reactions forming 2,3 -allenyl amines and three-component 
coupling via 2-alkynyl-1,4-diol dicarbonate  
 
Results and Discussion 
Initially, we tried to use 2 -alkynyl-1,4-diol dicarbonate 1a, 
phenylboronic acid 2a, and N-benzyl-p-toluenesulfonamide 3a as 
model substrates. When [Pd(allyl)Cl] 2, SPhos, and K 2CO3 (Table 1, 
entry 1) were employed, we were delighted to observe a 70% 
yield of 4aaa. With this result, various bases were examined (Ta -
ble 1, entries 2—4) and Cs2CO3 turned out to be the best affording 
an 80% yield of 4aaa. We then investigated the solvent effect: at 
first, we used MeCN, Et2O, 1,4-dioxane, THF, and EtOAc to replace 
DCE (Table 1, entries 5—9), however, neither of them contributed 
a better result. To our delight, we finally found that when toluene 
was used as solvent, it could improve the yield of 4aaa to 88% 
(Table 1, entry 10). Considering the possible impact of tempera -
ture on the reaction, the reaction was tried at 40 °C or 60 °C, 
however, lower yields of 4aaa were observed (Table 1, entries 11 
and 12).  Further optimization was focused on the ratio of reac -
tants: as the ratio of 1a : 2a : 3a was changed from 1.0  : 1.0 : 1.5 to 
1.2 : 1.2 : 1.0, however, there was no improvement of the yield of 
4aaa (Table 1, entry 13). Then we increased the concentration 
from 0.1 mol/L to 0.2 mol/L, and the yield of 4aaa was improved 
to 90% (Table 1, entry 14). Next, we recalibrated the ratio of 1a : 
2a : 3a at a concentration of 0.2 mol/L, and to our delight, when  
the ratio of  1a : 2a : 3a was changed to 1.0 : 1.1 : 1.5, the yield of 
4aaa was improved to 92% (Table 1, entry 15). Besides the ratio of 
the substrates, the loading of base was also optimized: applying 
1.0 equivalent of Cs 2CO3 only led to a slightly lowe r yield of 4aaa 
(Table 1, entry 16), thus, we chose to employ this modified reac -
tion conditions (Table 1, entry 16) as the standard.

With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we began to 
investigate the substrate scope of three components, respectively 
(Scheme 2). Firstly, the scope of amines 3 was surveyed: with the 
electron-withdrawing group p-toluenesulfonyl (Ts) as R 4, R 3 may 
be benzyl (3a—3c), allyl (3d), alkyl (3e), 1H-indole-3-ethyl (3f), and 
2-thienylmethyl (3g) affording the corresponding 2,3 -allenyl 
amines 4 in 68%—89% yields. When N-Ts aniline 3h was used as 
amine, the reaction afforded a 50% yield of 2,3 -allenyl amine 
4aah. With electron-donating groups in the  para-position of the 
benzene ring of the N-Ts aniline, the yields of 2,3 -allenyl amines 
4aai and 4aaj were improved to 60%—66%, while with electron - 
withdrawing group on the benzene ring, there was a significant 
decrease in the yield of corresponding 2,3 -allenyl amine 4aak 
(33%). For R4, p-nitrobenzenesulfonyl (3l) and methylsulfonyl (3m) 
worked while groups such as t-butyloxy carbonyl (Boc), ben-
zyloxycarbonyl (Cbz) and trifluoroacetyl failed to afford the corre-
sponding allenes. Besides, bis( tert-butoxycarbonyl)amine ( 3n) 
showed good reactivity affording a 61% yield of target allene 4aan. 
The structure of 4aan was further confirmed by X -ray single crys-
tal analysis.  We also tried phthalimide, dimethylsulfoximine, or 
benzophenone imine as the amine 3, separately. However, neither 
of them afforded the corresponding 2,3-allenyl amines 4. Next, we 
investigated the reactivity of simple alkyl amines: Diethylamine 3o

Scheme 5  Control experiments 
 
Based on these control experiments, we proposed a plausible 
mechanism as shown in Scheme 6a. Initially, the oxidative addi -
tion occurred between the catalytically active species Pd(0)L n and 
2-alkynyl-1,4-diol dicarbonate 1a. Allenyl palladium intermediate 
Int-I was generated exclusively, indicating that the oxidative addi-
tion occurred exclusively with the more sterically crowded C —O 
bond. Compared with  its regioisomer Int-I’, the steric effect be-
tween palladium and substituent groups may cause this regio - 
selectivity (Scheme 6b). After the transmetalation, allenyl phenyl 
palladium intermediate Int-II was afforded. Because of the stabil -
ity of the six-membered cyclic coordination, this intermediate pre-
ferred β-O elimination to form 1,2,3 -butatriene-coordinated pal -
ladium intermediate Int-III rather than reductive elimination, as 
supported by the absence of 2,3 -allenyl carbonate 9aa in the con-
trol experi ment (Scheme 5a). Then , a regioselective insertion 
would lead to the formation of methylene -π-allyl palladium spe -
cies Int-IV. Int-IV would be converted to 2,3 -allenyl methyl ether 
8aa via reductive elimination. However, the C —O bond in 8aa 
would be activa ted via coordination between PhB(OH) 2 and the 
oxygen atom of the OMe group in Int-V.[10] After the oxidative 
addition, methylene-π-allyl palladium species Int-IV was also re-
generated. Finally, 2,3-allenyl amine 4aaa was afforded via nucle -
ophilic attack of the deprotonated N-benzyl-p-toluenesulfonamide 
3a to Int-IV and the Pd(0) species was regenerated to finish the 
catalytic cycle. 
Scheme 6  Proposed mechanism

(Scheme 7) . However, most of them afforded a low yield and  a 
poor enantioselectivity for the  corresponding 2,3 -allenyl amine

Conclusions 
In conclusion, we have developed a palladium -catalyzed 
three-component coupling reaction to generate 2,3-allenyl amines 
with excellent regio- and chemo-selectivity. This reaction showed 
remarkable substrate tolerance of various 2 -alkynyl-1,4-diol di -
carbonate, organoboronic acid, and nitrogen nucleophiles. The 
synthetic potential of 2,3 -allenyl amines has been demonstrated. 
Control experiments supported our unique proposed mechanism 
involving 1,2,3-triene-palladium species  and methylene -π-allyl 
palladium species. Further studies on the regulation of enanti -
oselectivity of this reaction are  rather challenging and  ongoing in 
our laboratory. 
Experimental 
Typical procedure: To a flame-dried Schlenk tube were added 
[Pd(allyl)Cl]2 (0.025 mmol), Sphos (0.12 mmol), Cs2CO3 (1.0 mmol), 
1 (1.0 mmol), 2 (1.1 mmol), and 3 (1.5 mmol). After the addition, 
the Schlenk tube was degassed and refilled with argon for three 
times at room temperature by vacuum, and toluene (5 mL) was 
added. The resulting mixture was stirred at 50 °C for 24 h as mon-
itored by TLC. After cooling to room temperature, the resulting 
mixture was filtered through a short column of silica gel (3 cm) 
eluted with ethyl acetate (30 mL) and concentrated. The residue 
was purified by column chromatography on silica gel to afford the 
desired 2,3-allenyl amines 4.
